title: On Melt in the Contact Layers of M2 Steel in Dry Sliding Against C45 Steel Under High Density Alternating Electric Current
content: Developing new principles for control technical systems required the reliable actuators creation. A sliding steel/steel contact under high density electric current could be one of the elements for such actuators. The search for factors that caused wear reduction of such contacts should be a subject of scientific and commercial interest. One of such factors could be the melting that occurs in a sliding steel/steel electrical contact. The overall goal of this study was to describe the characteristics of an M2 steel/steel sliding electrical con-tact in the presence of melt. Dry sliding of M2 steel (sample) against C45 steel (counter-body) under a current density higher than 100 A/cm2 was performed as a model experi-ment using the well-known "pin-on-ring" tribo-loading configuration under alternating electric current. The tribolayer formation on the sample and counterbody was demon-strated applying a scanning electron microscope and a MICRO MEASURE 3D-station non-contact device. Accordingly to EDX analysis, the contact layers contained predomi-nantly oxygen and iron. Two sectors with different morphological features were observed on the M2 steel sliding surface. Melt formation as a new dissipative structure was visible in one of the sectors. A method for calculating the melt layer thickness was proposed. This thickness did not exceed 10 μm. The possibility of melt formation was demonstrated ex-perimentally and confirmed by this calculation. The melt amount increased with the cur-rent density increase and contributed to increase in the contact electric conductivity and to decrease in the friction coefficient. The proposed analysis of the obtained results could serve as a basis for broader generalizations.
